body.statement:
For every \(p\in\mathcal P\) and \(\gamma\in[-G,G]\), write \(P_{\gamma,t}\) for the stationary semigroup generated by \(\mathcal L_\gamma\).  The potential \(-\log\pi_\gamma\), up to its normalizing constant, is continuously differentiable and piecewise quadratic, with second derivative at least \(d/q\) away from \(\gamma\).  If \(f\) is locally absolutely continuous and \(f,f'\in L^2(\pi_\gamma)\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(f)
 \leq \frac qd\int_{\mathbb R}\{f'(x)\}^2\pi_\gamma(x)\,dx .
\]
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathcal P\) and \(\gamma\in[-G,G]\).  Put
\[
 b_\gamma(x)=-dx-\nu\min\{x,\gamma\}.
\]
The displayed density in the frozen core satisfies \(q(\log\pi_\gamma)'=b_\gamma\) on both sides of the kink.  The two one-sided derivatives agree at \(x=\gamma\), because each equals \(-D\gamma/q\).  Hence the potential \(U_\gamma=-\log\pi_\gamma\), with its additive normalizing constant suppressed, is continuously differentiable and
\[
 U_\gamma''(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 D/q,&x<\gamma,\\
 d/q,&x>\gamma.
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{1}
\]
The rate assumptions give \(D=d+\nu>d>0\) and \(q>0\), so (1) proves the asserted curvature bound.

Let \(X_t^x\) and \(X_t^y\) solve the diffusion equation with drift \(b_\gamma\), diffusion coefficient \(\sqrt{2q}\), initial states \(x,y\), and the same Brownian path.  Since \(u\mapsto\min\{u,\gamma\}\) is nondecreasing,
\[
 (x-y)\{b_\gamma(x)-b_\gamma(y)\}
 \leq-d(x-y)^2.                                                  \tag{2}
\]
The Brownian terms cancel under this synchronous coupling.  Applying the ordinary chain rule away from the zero set of the difference and integrating the resulting differential inequality gives
\[
 |X_t^x-X_t^y|\leq e^{-dt}|x-y|.                                \tag{3}
\]
For smooth compactly supported \(f\), difference quotients in the initial state and (3) imply
\[
 |(P_{\gamma,t}f)'(x)|
 \leq e^{-dt}P_{\gamma,t}|f'|(x).                               \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, the stochastic flow derivative exists off the null set of paths hitting the single nondifferentiability point at the differentiation instant, is bounded by \(e^{-dt}\), and approximation of the Lipschitz drift by drifts with slopes in \([-D,-d]\) gives (4) without an exceptional initial state.  Jensen's inequality and invariance of \(\pi_\gamma\) therefore yield
\[
 \int\{(P_{\gamma,t}f)'\}^2\,d\pi_\gamma
 \leq e^{-2dt}\int P_{\gamma,t}(f'^2)\,d\pi_\gamma
 =e^{-2dt}\int f'^2\,d\pi_\gamma.                              \tag{5}
\]

The identity \(q(\log\pi_\gamma)'=b_\gamma\), integration by parts on the two half-lines, and continuity at the kink show that
\[
 -\int u\mathcal L_\gamma v\,d\pi_\gamma
 =q\int u'v'\,d\pi_\gamma                                    \tag{6}
\]
for smooth compactly supported \(u,v\); the boundary terms at \(\gamma\) cancel.  Apply (6) with \(u=v=P_{\gamma,t}f\).  Stationarity and the semigroup equation give
\[
 -\frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(P_{\gamma,t}f)
 =2q\int\{(P_{\gamma,t}f)'\}^2\,d\pi_\gamma.                 \tag{7}
\]
For compactly supported Lipschitz \(f\), (3), coupled with an independent stationary initial state, shows that \(P_{\gamma,t}f\) converges in \(L^2(\pi_\gamma)\) to \(\int f\,d\pi_\gamma\); the Gaussian tails of the displayed invariant density make the coupling's second moment finite.  Integrating (7) from zero to infinity and then using (5) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(f)
 &=2q\int_0^\infty\int\{(P_{\gamma,t}f)'\}^2\,d\pi_\gamma\,dt\\
 &\leq2q\int_0^\infty e^{-2dt}\,dt
       \int(f')^2\,d\pi_\gamma
 =\frac qd\int(f')^2\,d\pi_\gamma.                            \tag{8}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Finally, truncate and mollify an arbitrary locally absolutely continuous \(f\) with \(f,f'\in L^2(\pi_\gamma)\).  Both sides of (8) converge by the \(L^2(\pi_\gamma)\) convergence of the functions and their derivatives.  This proves the stated inequality.
